guide_enrichment.narrative:
The market is asking Missouri to create slightly more separation than our model expects, and Florida’s rushing offense is the clearest reason for that difference. Jadan Baugh produced 458 yards and eight rushing touchdowns through three games, while Florida’s six consecutive scoring drives at Auburn showed it could sustain offense on the road. We are not treating one performance as proof, but the underlying rushing efficiency gives Florida a credible way to shorten the game and avoid obvious passing situations.

The counter is Missouri’s ability to prevent scoring opportunities and limit efficient passing, two areas that challenge Florida’s offense beyond the ground game. We also note that Missouri entered the season with only two returning defensive starters after losing 10, which adds some uncertainty to how sustainable that early defensive profile will be. Our numbers still favor Missouri, but the football case for Florida staying competitive is strong enough to narrow the expected margin—not strong enough to create value at the available price.
guide_enrichment.matchup_to_watch: For us, Florida’s rushing offense against Missouri’s run defense is the matchup that can shape the spread. Our numbers rate the ground game as Florida’s clearest offensive advantage, while Missouri has been less convincing against the run than in overall scoring-opportunity prevention. If Florida keeps Baugh productive and stays on schedule, Missouri may have fewer chances to lean on its stronger pass defense; if Missouri controls early downs, the matchup shifts toward the home side’s defensive strengths.

recent_game.fact: Florida improved to 3-0 and 1-0 in SEC play with a 44-39 road win at Auburn on September 19.
Florida produced six consecutive scoring drives from the first quarter through the third quarter at Auburn, with five consecutive drives covering at least 65 yards.
Jadan Baugh rushed for 162 yards at Auburn, his fourth consecutive 100-yard rushing game.
Aaron Philo completed 15 of 22 passes for 204 yards, one touchdown and one interception in his first road game as a Gator.
Florida recorded seven sacks at Auburn after totaling four sacks over its first two games.
Florida held Auburn to minus-3 total yards, no first downs and an 0-for-4 passing line with one interception in the first quarter.
Jayden Woods had six tackles, 3.5 tackles for loss and 2.5 sacks at Auburn.
Cormani McClain intercepted Auburn's second pass attempt on its opening drive.

quarterback.fact: Aaron Philo completed 47 of 64 passes for 721 yards, six touchdowns and two interceptions through Florida's first three games.

Philo also scored two rushing touchdowns through three games.

recent_game.fact: Missouri opened the 2026 season with a 54-14 victory over Arkansas-Pine Bluff on September 3.
Missouri produced 562 total yards against Arkansas-Pine Bluff, including 357 passing and 205 rushing, while allowing 198 total yards.
Missouri led Arkansas-Pine Bluff 40-0 at halftime and held a 376-6 yardage advantage through the first two quarters.
Missouri converted 6 of 10 third downs, both fourth-down attempts and all five red-zone possessions against Arkansas-Pine Bluff.

opponent_notes.fact: Missouri's schedule lists Florida as a home SEC opponent on October 3, 2026; Florida was receiving votes in both major polls when these notes were issued.

quarterback.fact: Ole Miss transfer Austin Simmons started the opener and completed 17 of 19 passes for 252 yards, four touchdowns and no interceptions.
Simmons' 89.5 completion percentage and 270.4 passer rating were Missouri records for a quarterback making his Tigers debut.
Simmons is the seventh quarterback to start for Missouri during Eli Drinkwitz's tenure and the third transfer quarterback.
Sophomore Matt Zollers was listed as Simmons' backup and completed 8 of 12 passes for 87 yards while adding a five-yard rushing touchdown in the opener.

offensive_personnel.fact: Missouri's listed first-team offensive line was LT Cayden Green, LG Tristan Wilson, C Dominick Giudice, RG Curtis Peagler and RT Luke Work.
Green, Giudice and Peagler returned from the 2025 starting offensive line, while center Connor Tollison and tackle Keagen Trost were among the departed starters.
Cayden Green recorded no participation in the season opener despite being listed as the first-team left tackle on the subsequent depth chart.
Running back Jamal Roberts started the opener and led Missouri with 13 carries for 47 yards and one touchdown.
Returning 1,649-yard rusher Ahmad Hardy recorded no participation in the season opener.
Ole Miss transfer Cayden Lee started at receiver and caught five passes for 89 yards, including a 47-yard touchdown, in his Missouri debut.
Sophomore receiver Donovan Olugbode set career highs with seven receptions, 107 yards and two touchdowns in the opener.

defensive_personnel.fact: Missouri entered 2026 with two returning defensive starters and 10 lost defensive starters.
Linebacker Nicholas Rodriguez and safety Santana Banner ranked second and third on Missouri in tackles in 2025 and returned for 2026.
Defensive tackles Marquis Gracial and Sterling Webb returned after combining for 6.0 tackles for loss in 2025; Webb also had 2.5 sacks and six quarterback hurries.
Edge defender Darris Smith returned after recording 4.0 sacks as a pass-rush specialist in 2025 and was listed as a first-team JACK for 2026.
Auburn transfer Robert Woodyard Jr. started at middle linebacker after making 11 starts and recording 67 tackles for Auburn in 2025.
Ole Miss transfer Chris Graves Jr. started at cornerback after appearing in 41 games with nine starts for the Rebels over the previous three seasons.

coaching_changes.fact: Chip Lindsey joined Missouri as offensive coordinator in December 2025 and is in his first season in the role.
Garrett Riley joined Missouri in January 2026 as quarterbacks coach after serving as Clemson's offensive coordinator and quarterbacks coach.
John Papuchis became Missouri's special teams coordinator and defensive assistant in January 2026 after six seasons coordinating Florida State's special teams.
Derek Nicholson added co-defensive coordinator duties before the 2026 season while continuing to coach linebackers.
Alex Atkins joined Missouri in January 2026 as tight ends coach, and Chop Harbin joined as defensive line coach.
